chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah, from Isa ibn Abdullah al-Umari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

key_terms.طَلَبُ الْعِلْمِ: The seeking or pursuit of knowledge — used as a technical phrase emphasizing that one must actively pursue knowledge, not merely receive it passively.
key_terms.فَرِيضَةٌ: An obligation/duty (farida) — a legally and religiously binding act, carrying the same weight as prayer and fasting in Islamic law.

ai.seo_question: Is seeking knowledge obligatory in Islam according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith transmits a concise but weighty declaration from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS): that the pursuit of knowledge is not optional or praiseworthy merely, but an obligation (farida) incumbent upon every believer. The use of the word farida — the same word used for obligatory prayer and fasting — signals that acquiring religious and intellectual knowledge carries the same binding weight as other core Islamic duties. This teaching would have been understood by the Imam's contemporaries as a counter to both ignorance and to any quietist tendency that might lead believers to neglect learning.
